original_question: Define a notion of alternating virtual knot, classify alternating virtual knots and alternating weaves on surfaces without stabilization, and formulate and prove the virtual analogue of the Tait flyping conjecture.
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the three components of the paper's target problem: introduce a notion of alternation in the virtual setting, classify alternating virtual knots, and formulate/prove a Tait-flyping-type statement; it also correctly preserves the separate surface-level clause and the restriction 'without stabilization'.
missing_details: Make the ambient setting explicit: in the paper, virtual knots are taken in the standard virtual-knot sense of diagrams modulo the generalized Reidemeister moves, equivalently as stable equivalence classes of knot embeddings in thickened compact oriented surfaces.
State explicitly that 'alternating' is itself part of what must be defined; the paper does not supply a prior formal definition here.

Clarify that the surface clause is separate from the virtual-knot clause: one must classify all alternating weaves on fixed surfaces before quotienting by addition/removal of empty handles, i.e. without stabilization.
Keep the first classification clause at the level of virtual knots, as in item 15, rather than silently broadening it to a general classification of all virtual links.
The paper says to find an analogue of the Tait flyping conjecture and prove it, so the refined question should not presuppose a specific pre-existing virtual flyping statement.
No ring, field, grading, homogeneity, or degree restrictions are part of this problem; adding such data would move away from the paper's actual scope.
refined_question: In virtual knot theory, where virtual knots are considered up to the generalized Reidemeister moves and equivalently as stable equivalence classes of knot embeddings in thickened compact oriented surfaces, define a notion of alternating virtual knot, classify the alternating virtual knots, classify all alternating weaves on fixed compact oriented surfaces before stabilization (that is, without adding or removing empty handles), and formulate and prove the appropriate analogue of the classical Tait flyping conjecture in this virtual/surface setting.
justification: The draft is very close to the paper's official formulation and is clearly aimed at Section 8.1, item 15. The main sharpening needed to make it stand-alone and paper-faithful is to spell out the ambient virtual-knot/surface framework from Sections 2.1 and 2.3, while preserving the paper's separate clause about classifying alternating surface weaves without stabilization. The wording 'weaves on surfaces' is worth retaining because Section 2.2 uses 'weaving' for the over/under structure of a shadow diagram, and item 15 then asks for the alternating surface classification before stabilization. The nearby item 16 supplies the immediate classical comparison by recalling the minimality theorem for ordinary alternating diagrams and by shifting attention to projections on higher-genus surfaces, which is why the refined question keeps the surface viewpoint explicit.
